description: ByteDance / TikTok runs a strict one-round-at-a-time funnel with sharp org-by-org variance in bar, language, and round mix. Coding rounds skew toward classic LeetCode-medium with one self-built test case; MLE and SRE loops front-load 30+ minutes of oral 八股 before any code is written. Interviewer professionalism varies — strong candidates drive the round structurally rather than waiting to be assessed.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: Number of Islands and Grid BFS Variants
questions.overview: Grid traversal in the 'number of islands' family — count connected components, then a follow-up that adds a constraint such as no-modify-in-place, equal-shape detection, water-flow direction, or 2D scaling.

questions.title: LRU Cache (with TTL and LFU Follow-ups)
questions.overview: Design and implement an LRU cache in O(1) per op. Follow-ups extend it with TTL expiry, LFU eviction, or fixed-time get/put semantics under contention.

questions.title: Basic Calculator (with and without parentheses)
questions.overview: Implement a string calculator supporting +, -, *, / on integers. Variants range from no-parentheses (operator precedence only) to full infix with parentheses and unary minus.

questions.title: Merge Intervals
questions.overview: The canonical LeetCode 56 prompt: merge every overlapping interval and return the non-overlapping intervals that cover the same ranges.

questions.title: Course Schedule and Topological Sort on a Directed Graph
questions.overview: Detect whether a directed-graph schedule is satisfiable (cycle detection on a DAG), then extend to producing a valid order — used both as a SWE coding question and as the warmup before a word-ladder shortest-path follow-up.

questions.title: Reverse Nodes in K-Group (incomplete tail variant)
questions.overview: Reverse a linked list in groups of K. Variants flip the convention for the final partial group, split into a two-step problem (single-list reverse warmup first, then grouped reverse), or invert the task entirely — reverse the order of the K-groups while keeping each group's internal order intact.

questions.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (with path reconstruction)
questions.overview: Classic 'max path sum that may bend at any node' on a binary tree, plus the harder follow-up of reconstructing the actual node sequence — not just the score.

questions.title: Seller Task Scheduler
questions.overview: Implement task intake and next-task selection with per-seller priority ordering and tier-weighted turns across sellers.

questions.title: Timestamped Task Scheduler
questions.overview: Implement a task scheduler supporting `addTask(taskID, timestamp)`, `removeTask(taskID)`, and `popTask(num)`, where `popTask` removes and returns the first `num` tasks ordered by start timestamp.

questions.title: Pythagorean Triple in an Integer Array
questions.overview: Given an integer array, decide whether three available elements can be chosen as a, b, and c such that a² + b² = c². Negative values, zero, and duplicate counts all matter; the expected general bound discussed in the round was quadratic time.

questions.title: Stickers to Spell Word (LeetCode 691)
questions.overview: Given reusable letter stickers and a target string, return the minimum number of stickers needed to assemble the target. The prompt was identified as LeetCode 691, with the target length limited to roughly the low teens.

questions.title: Minimum Window Substring (LeetCode 76)
questions.overview: Find the shortest substring of S containing every character of T with multiplicity, then handle variants requiring a threshold count and returning all equally short answers. The prompt was identified as LeetCode 76.

questions.title: Build a Nested Comment Tree from Flat Records
questions.overview: Transform a flat list of comment objects with id, parent_id, and text into a nested root array by attaching children recursively. The supplied example contains two roots and a grandchild, plus a parent_id typo in the displayed expected payload that should be clarified.

questions.title: AI-Assisted Order Validator
questions.overview: Build an `OrderValidator` that rejects prohibited items and out-of-range prices, supports adding and removing validation rules, and respects dependencies between rules. The follow-up changes the dependency graph when a rule is removed: its prerequisites become prerequisites of its downstream rules.

questions.title: Bounded Number Construction from Allowed Digits
questions.overview: Given an integer N and a set A of decimal digits reusable without limit, construct the largest number strictly smaller than N using only digits from A. One interview example uses N = 23415 and A = {2, 4, 9}, producing 22999.

questions.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
questions.overview: The unmodified LeetCode 424 prompt: replace at most `k` characters in an uppercase string and return the longest substring that can be made entirely one repeated character.

questions.title: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.overview: The unmodified LeetCode 239 prompt: given an integer array and a fixed window size, return the maximum value in every window as it advances one position at a time.

questions.title: Flatten a Multilevel Doubly Linked List (Skip Empty Nodes)
questions.overview: LC 430 (Flatten a Multilevel Doubly Linked List) with one delta: nested nodes carry empty values and must be excluded from the flattened output. Asked alongside a binary-tree max-path-sum question in the same IC round.

questions.title: Equalize Root-to-Leaf Path Sums in an N-ary Tree
questions.overview: After a warm-up (most frequent array element, ties broken toward the smaller number), the main problem gives an n-ary tree of integers where each operation increments one node's value by 1; return the minimum operations to make all root-to-leaf path sums equal. Both problems require self-written, executed test cases.

questions.title: Grid Shortest Path with K Obstacle Eliminations
questions.overview: First-round Growth coding prompt: find the shortest path in a grid, then handle the follow-up where up to `k` obstacles can be eliminated. Full I/O was thin, but the required state is `(row, col, remaining_eliminations)` for the follow-up.

questions.title: Elements Appearing More Than n/3 in a Sorted Array
questions.overview: Given a sorted array of length at least 3, return every value whose frequency is greater than `n / 3`. Examples include `[1,1,2,4,4] -> [1,4]`; follow-up requires time complexity below `O(n)` by exploiting sorted order.

questions.title: Longest Zigzag Path in a Grid
questions.overview: TT Ads phone screen. Given an integer grid, return the length of the longest path (4-directional moves) whose consecutive value comparisons strictly alternate — grid[a] < grid[b] > grid[c] < ... or the inverse. DFS over a (cell, last-direction) state, best memoized like a longest-increasing-path-in-matrix DP; solved with DFS + backtracking.

questions.title: N-ary Tree Path Sum Count
questions.overview: Count target-sum paths in a tree, with the binary-tree version generalized to an N-ary tree. The expected optimal solution uses DFS plus a prefix-sum counter rather than checking every ancestor path.

questions.title: Word Search II with Trie
questions.overview: Find words from a dictionary inside a 2D character board. The expected solution builds a trie over the word list, then runs backtracking DFS from each board cell with in-place visited marking.

questions.title: Minimum-Cost Path on a Grid with Fuel and Recharge Cells
questions.overview: Weighted-cost grid traversal from top-left to bottom-right with a fuel budget that depletes per step, can be refilled at marked cells, and is bounded by some cells being fully blocked.

questions.title: Reverse Words in a String (Preserve Spaces, In-Place)
questions.overview: Reverse the word order in a string. Follow-ups: rewrite to preserve the original number of spaces between every position, and reduce extra space below `O(n)`.

questions.title: Photo Groups via Transitive Similarity
questions.overview: Given a symmetric similarity matrix where `isSimilar[i][j] == 1` means photos i and j are directly similar, count the number of photo groups under transitive closure.

questions.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
questions.overview: Standard tree-from-the-right view problem, but reported with the extra constraint of building the input tree yourself and writing all test scaffolding inside the round.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses with Wildcard '*' and DFS All Strings
questions.overview: Validate a parenthesis string where `*` can act as `(`, `)`, or empty. Follow-up: enumerate every valid concrete string the input can produce.

questions.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
questions.overview: Given a histogram represented by an array of bar heights, compute the largest rectangular area contained inside it. Reported as the second problem in an NG SWE phone screen after a sliding-window warmup.

questions.title: CodeSignal ML / Research Scientist OA (10-Problem Battery)
questions.overview: 10-question, 70-minute CodeSignal battery for ByteDance Research Scientist intern: a mix of ML multiple-choice on classical model trade-offs, a hand-computed forward pass, a local-maximum array algorithm, and from-scratch implementations of Bagging and k-Means.

questions.title: Contiguous Subarray with Largest Min + Max
questions.overview: A custom 30-minute coding question: given a positive integer array, find a contiguous subarray (length ≥ 2) maximizing `min + max`, return the sum.

questions.title: Subarray Sum Equals K (Count)
questions.overview: Given an integer array and a target `k`, return the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals `k`. The exact interview signature, constraints, and examples remain unspecified.

questions.title: Create Binary Tree from Descriptions (LeetCode 2196)
questions.overview: Construct a binary tree from descriptions.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.overview: Given a string, return the length of its longest substring containing no repeated characters. The exact interview signature, character set, constraints, and examples remain unspecified.

questions.title: Intersection of Two Interval Lists
questions.overview: Given two interval lists, return their intersections. The prompt aligns with LC 986, while the interview report leaves sorting guarantees, endpoint semantics, and the exact output contract unspecified.

questions.title: Reconstruct Binary Tree from Preorder and Postorder
questions.overview: Reconstruct a binary tree from its preorder and postorder traversals. The prompt aligns with LC 889, but the interview report does not specify uniqueness assumptions or the exact return contract.

questions.title: Reverse a Linked List In Place
questions.overview: Reverse a linked list in place.

questions.title: Non-Overlapping Intervals (LeetCode 435)
questions.overview: Find the minimum removals needed to eliminate overlapping intervals.

questions.title: Time Based Key-Value Store (LeetCode 981)
questions.overview: Implement time-indexed key-value storage.

questions.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
questions.overview: Sliding-window warmup in a TT SDE phone screen, paired with a much harder grid-with-fuel BFS problem.

questions.title: Restore IP Addresses
questions.overview: Partition a digit string into every valid IPv4 address: exactly four numeric segments, each valid and with no leading zero unless the segment itself is zero. The follow-up generalizes the partition to an arbitrary `k` supplied as another argument.

questions.title: Alien Dictionary
questions.overview: The standard Alien Dictionary problem: infer a valid character order from words already sorted under an unknown alphabet. The implementation must include every character, avoid duplicate indegree increments, detect impossible ordering constraints, and explain each graph update.

questions.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
questions.overview: LeetCode 33: search for a target in an ascending array rotated at an unknown pivot and return its index or `-1`. A current intern-screen follow-up removes the distinct-values guarantee, requiring explicit handling of duplicate boundary values.

questions.title: MinStack, MaxStack and Streaming Median
questions.overview: Three linked structures in a single MLE round: `MinStack` with O(1) min, `MaxStack`, and a streaming-median follow-up that pushes you to two heaps — then asks how to retrofit `MaxStack` to maintain the running median.

questions.title: Remove Duplicate Letters for Lexicographically Smallest Result
questions.overview: Given a string, remove duplicate letters so each character appears exactly once and the final string is lexicographically smallest among all valid results. The round explicitly included the two standard examples `bcabc -> abc` and `cbacdcbc -> acdb`, with a monotonic-stack solution expected.

questions.title: Hand-Code Self-Attention and Cross-Entropy
questions.overview: Write self-attention pseudocode and the cross-entropy loss derivation on the spot, interleaved with attention-mechanism oral questions (FFN role, attention scaling).

questions.title: CodeSignal SWE OA (Spring 2026 Bank)
questions.overview: TikTok's Spring 2026 SWE intern OA on CodeSignal: 4 problems covering memory allocator simulation, alternating-parity zigzag counting, charging-station relay, and constrained text justification.

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Substring (LeetCode 5)
questions.overview: Return the longest contiguous palindromic substring. A follow-up requires Manacher's algorithm rather than the classic expand-around-center baseline.

questions.title: LeetCode 20 Valid Parentheses in SRE Loop
questions.overview: Validate parentheses in a short SRE coding exercise and run the test cases.

questions.title: Content Moderation System Design
questions.overview: End-to-end design of a content-moderation pipeline for short-video / e-commerce content. Variants include ML inference layer, feature pipeline, job scheduler follow-up, and review-queue prioritization.

questions.title: Top Songs by Country Leaderboard
questions.overview: Design a near-real-time service that ingests song listen/click events and serves each country's top ten songs, refreshing about every ten minutes. The stated scale is roughly 500 million users and about 50K read QPS plus 50K event writes per second, with availability favored over strong consistency.

questions.title: AI-Driven QA Pipeline Workflow
questions.overview: Design an AI-oriented QA workflow that turns a PRD into test cases, test data, automation scripts, execution, and a final report. The interviewer expects collaborating role-specific agents rather than merely inserting model calls into conventional CI stages, and asks how the system operates when CI has no GPU capacity.

questions.title: Recent Like Count and Top Posts in a Sliding Window
questions.overview: Design the last-minute like-count backend for a social platform: exact count for one post, global top posts over the last minute, and region-based top posts over the same window.

questions.title: Realtime Auction Bidding System
questions.overview: Design a high-read, high-write auction service with REST bids, ordered bid processing, durable bid history, current-price state, and realtime client updates through SSE or WebSocket.

questions.title: Agent Tool-Use System Design (AML Volcano Engine)
questions.overview: Senior research-scientist intern round at ByteDance AML (Volcano Engine): open-ended design of an agent tool-use system, drilling on state management, evaluation, and failure modes of multi-step tool-invoking agents.

questions.title: ML System Design: Dynamic K in Retrieval Stage
questions.overview: Open-ended ML system design for a senior / staff MLE round: in a recommendation stack, design a model or system to dynamically determine `K` — the number of candidates passed from retrieval to ranking — per request, rather than using a static cap.

questions.title: Design a Stripe-like Payment Platform
questions.overview: Open-ended payment-platform system design for an SRE candidate: payment intent lifecycle, idempotency, transactional integrity, retry semantics under partial failure.

questions.title: Short-Video Recommendation System
questions.overview: Design a multi-stage short-video recommendation stack: parallel retrieval produces hundreds to thousands of candidates per route, coarse ranking reduces the pool, fine ranking optimizes several engagement objectives, and reranking enforces diversity and exploration. Deep dives cover cold start, event-time feature correctness, real-time behavior updates, and online evaluation.

questions.title: Video-Keyword Association Review System
questions.overview: Design a service where users submit batches of 50+ videos and 1000+ keywords, then the system evaluates association between videos and keywords while supporting updates, versioning, and resumable upload.

questions.title: Project Deep Dive (Resume Drill)
questions.overview: Most rounds open with 15-30 minutes of resume deep-dive before any coding. Interviewers anchor on one project from your resume, drill into the technical decisions, and probe `why this trade-off, not that one`.

questions.title: Hiring Manager / Final Behavioral Round
questions.overview: Final HM round, typically 30-45 min, mixing standard STAR-format behavioral questions with one extra project deep-dive — and on the director / M2 variant, motivation and impact rather than implementation details.

questions.title: Data Engineering Experience Screen
questions.overview: A recruiter screen follows a previously completed experience form, covering data modeling, warehouses, and data services.

questions.title: Motivation, Ambiguity, and Collaboration Screen
questions.overview: Prepare concise answers for why you are changing roles, difficult project communication, handling ambiguity, personal weakness, acceptable work pace, and cross-time-zone constraints. These questions appear inside technical phone screens rather than only in the final HM round.

questions.title: SRE Linux / Networking Troubleshooting Round
questions.overview: Verbal round for SRE and network-focused SDE candidates drilling Linux internals, networking, and structured production triage. Recurring topics include disk-full RCA, slow-backend triage, browser-to-backend connectivity, HTTP / DNS / TCP fundamentals, and packet sizing.

questions.title: MLE Oral 八股: Dropout, Overfitting, Normalization, Loss Functions
questions.overview: Oral ML-fundamentals quiz that runs at the front of nearly every MLE / Monetization / Commerce phone screen. Topics rotate but the deep-dive targets are stable: dropout mechanics, overfitting mitigation, normalization choices, and standard loss functions.

questions.title: CAP / DB Indexing / Concurrency / Logging Oral 八股
questions.overview: Backend oral cluster covering schema and index choices, CAP trade-offs, cache failure modes, messaging, web transport, SQL-versus-document storage, concurrency, and production logging.

questions.title: LLM Safety Project Deep Dive
questions.overview: A senior USDS JV MLE technical discussion probes LLM safety post-training ownership, escalation, design choices, and multimodal safety trade-offs.

questions.title: AI Agent Intern Technical Questions
questions.overview: A Chinese-language AI Agent internship screen combines virtual-memory and TCP questions with agent-quality evaluation and tool-call debugging.

questions.title: RAG / Agent / Kafka Oral Drill
questions.overview: A verbal fundamentals screen covering RAG, LangGraph / LangChain agent design, tool use, MCP, Kafka consumer groups, Redis / MySQL persistence, concurrency, and long-context memory handling.
